open_decision: The laws do not fix the order of the new entries after the old registry, and they do not forbid repeated copies of a new entry.
input: enable=false, locked=none; starter list [{id 1, adapter 1, model 1, enabled true}, {id 2, adapter 2, model 2, enabled true}]; registry []
result_a: [{id 1, adapter 1, model 1, enabled false}, {id 2, adapter 2, model 2, enabled false}] (starter order, as ref)

reason: Every law about the tail t only talks about membership of t, so a design that reverses t passes all laws. The registries differ as lists, and sentence 6 says only that new entries go to the end.
